The tables detfield::bin_detections() takes

Source: R/to_detfield.R
as_detfield_input.Rd

Returns the detections, listening and tag_delay inputs of detfield::bin_detections() from a detset, with the names detfield reads. detqc and detfield do not import each other; they meet through these tables. Two inputs are often missing from real files, and bin_detections() stops until they are given: transmission delays (network exports carry none; see tag_delay below), and codes, how the codes of a tag that sends two are counted (see detfield::bin_detections()).

Usage

as_detfield_input(
  x,
  listening = c("both", "days", "deployments"),
  stations = NULL,
  extent = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A detset.

listening

"both", "days" or "deployments".

stations

Optional station_id values to keep.

extent

Optional c(lon_min, lon_max, lat_min, lat_max), decimal degrees, WGS 84: keep the deployments whose position lies inside.

Value

A list of detections, listening and tag_delay.

Details

  • detections: datetime, receiver_serial, transmitter, animal_id and station_id. Rows with no animal_id, such as reference tags, are kept; bin_detections() leaves them out.

  • listening: by default list(deployments = , days = ), the form in which a receiver listens in a bin when its deployment covers the bin and the bin's UTC date is a listed day. Each deployment ends at its recover_datetime or its download_datetime, whichever comes first: the set holds no data after a download, so the hours after it on the download day are not listening. A deployment with no recovery time ends where the same receiver is deployed again. A detection after the recorded download keeps the end at the download: the detection is returned, and detfield::bin_detections() gives its rows listening = FALSE. A message counts such detections in the tables returned; they are the rows detset() marks in after_download. With a listening table from audit_listening(), each deployment ends where the audit ended it. The default list and the days table alone can differ by a few receiver-days and hourly rows on the first and last day of a deployment, and at a station whose deployments overlap, where the hourly rows take the serial of one of them. On the first and last day, the days table lists whole UTC days and the deployments table starts and ends at the recorded times. days is x$listening, with the logical column listening that audit_listening() writes: a day whose receiver was not downloaded, did not hear its own reference tag, or falls in a silent run, is not used, nor, with receiver logs, a day the receiver was "deaf" or "off"; a silent day, and a "logging_silent" one, counts as listening. listening = "days" or "deployments" gives one form alone.

  • tag_delay: transmitter, animal_id, min_delay and max_delay from the animals table, for transmitters with both delays; NULL, with a message, when none has them. read_animals() with tag_specs fills the delays from the manufacturer's sheet. Otherwise give tag_delay to bin_detections() yourself.

Network receiver files. A GLATOS or OTN receiver file lists every receiver in the network, so every bin would list thousands of receivers in other lakes as silent listeners, and detfield::location_surface() stops on listening receivers its field does not hold. Give stations, such as the receivers of a field keyed by station_id, or extent, to keep only those deployments with their detections and listening days. A message counts what was kept, and, with neither given, says so when the deployments name more than ten times as many stations as heard anything.

Examples

study <- detqc_example
dets <- detset(study$detections, study$deployments, study$animals)
detfield_input <- as_detfield_input(dets, listening = "days")
head(detfield_input$detections, 3)
#>              datetime receiver_serial    transmitter animal_id station_id
#> 1 2024-06-02 15:50:39            R012 A69-9002-61002     ST-02       S012
#> 2 2024-06-02 15:54:59            R012 A69-9002-61002     ST-02       S012
#> 3 2024-06-02 15:56:56            R009 A69-1601-61004     ST-04       S009
head(detfield_input$listening)
#>   receiver_serial station_id       date
#> 1            R001       S001 2024-06-01
#> 2            R001       S001 2024-06-02
#> 3            R001       S001 2024-06-03
#> 4            R001       S001 2024-06-04
#> 5            R001       S001 2024-06-05
#> 6            R001       S001 2024-06-06
# Keep two_stations stations only, as for a field built on them.
two_stations <- as_detfield_input(dets, stations = c("S010", "S011"))
#> as_detfield_input(): kept 2 of 20 deployments, 1,620 of 3,297 detections
#> and 22 of 220 receiver-days at the stations given.
